extraction.name: SCIENCE QA (Science Question Answering)
extraction.description: SCIENCE QA is a multimodal multiple-choice science question answering benchmark consisting of 21,208 examples sourced from elementary and high school science curricula across natural science, social science, and language science. Questions are annotated with corresponding lectures and detailed explanations revealing step-by-step chains of thought.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan
extraction.citeAs: Lu, P., Mishra, S., Xia, T., Qiu, L., Chang, K.-W., Zhu, S.-C., Tafjord, O., Clark, P., & Kalyan, A. (2022). Learn to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022).
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions in the dataset were sourced from open educational resources managed by IXL Learning that align with California Common Core Content Standards. The original science problems were downloaded, and individual components (questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted using heuristic rules.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Not all questions contain every modality or component: 7,188 questions (33.9%) lack context, 10,876 questions lack image context, 10,988 questions lack text context, 3,410 questions (16.1%) lack a lecture, and 2,006 questions (9.5%) lack an explanation. For questions without context, the context text is replaced with an empty string.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Open resources managed by IXL Learning (https://www.ixl.com/), an online learning platform curated by experts in the field of K-12 education.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: For questions without any context, the context text is replaced with an empty string.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Invalid questions were manually removed (e.g., questions with only one choice, faulty data, or duplicate questions). If multiple correct answers applied, only one was retained. Answer choices were shuffled for each question to prevent positional bias.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions so special structures such as tables and lists are distinguishable from simple text passages. For language models, newline separators (\n) were replaced with \\n. A visual captioning tool was used to generate text captions for images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions, answers, lectures, and explanations originated from K-12 education curricula curated by IXL Learning experts. A custom exploration tool (https://scienceqa.github.io/explore.html) was developed to review examples, and incorrect annotations were manually revised by experts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation scores for model-generated explanations (relevance, correctness, completeness) were determined via majority vote across three worker annotations per batch item.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk crowd workers who obtained a high school or higher degree and passed qualification exam examples.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The collected data does not contain any user usage data or personally identifiable/sensitive information such as gender and race.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Proposed to diagnose multimodal understanding and multi-hop reasoning abilities of AI systems and contribute to the development of K-12 education applications like tutoring systems. The authors state an adherence to AI for the common good and commit to removing any antisocial data points based on feedback.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: After careful examination, the authors reported finding no improper content such as pornographic information, racial remarks, or harmful social bias.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Model reasoning fails when context captions lack fine-grained semantics or fail on diagrams; language models struggle on questions requiring complex, uncommon domain knowledge or generate incorrect/incomplete chains of thought.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking multimodal learning, multi-hop reasoning, chain-of-thought generation, few-shot learning, and fine-tuning in AI systems; developing educational applications such as tutoring systems. The dataset is split into training (12,726), validation (4,241), and test (4,241) sets.
